priorIterationFindingReconfirmation.FIND-1701:
GENUINELY RESOLVED. Confirmed by a full, independent, fresh end-to-end read of both spec files (behavioral-spec.md:1-2876, verification-architecture.md:1-987 -- every REQ-101 through REQ-403, the complete Purity Boundary Map, all Proof Obligation rows, and the full Gate). REQ-102 (behavioral-spec.md:873-899) now states explicitly that `colonySurplusUsd` 'is never hand-assembled by the calling orchestration -- it is ALWAYS the DIRECT return value of THAT SAME evaluation's `computeColonySurplusUsd({citizens: filterProductiveCitizens(...), perCitizenReserveUsd})` call', with the identical binding sentence repeated in REQ-102's own Acceptance Criteria (behavioral-spec.md:1020-1027), and the explicit requirement that 'EACH separate `decideColonySpawn` evaluation within one wake cycle MUST call `computeColonySurplusUsd` fresh' (behavioral-spec.md:888-899). New proof obligation PROP-102k (verification-architecture.md:404) requires both a Tier-1 control-flow read and a Tier-2 integration test with a second fixture that mutates the underlying ledger/registry data BETWEEN two evaluations in the same simulated wake, confirming the SECOND evaluation's colonySurplusUsd reflects the freshly-recomputed value rather than the first evaluation's cached aggregate -- this mirrors PROP-101j/PROP-102g/PROP-102i/PROP-202d's exact shape, not a vague restatement. The Purity Boundary Map's decideColonySpawn row (verification-architecture.md:219) and the Gate's item (1) (verification-architecture.md:689-697) are both extended to cite this binding and this proof obligation.

CRITICALLY (per this iteration's own dispatch instruction to independently re-verify the safety claim about REQ-103's lock scope before trusting it, to avoid repeating this spec's own earlier FIND-501 mistake for a different mechanism): I independently re-read REQ-103's own current text (behavioral-spec.md:1095-1098) before accepting the resolution's honesty. It states verbatim: 'REQ-101's earlier registry read and REQ-102's decision themselves run OUTSIDE the lock, since REQ-102's gate function is pure and needs no mutual exclusion of its own ... only the ACT of proceeding on a true decision needs the lock.' This directly and accurately confirms REQ-102's own new claim (behavioral-spec.md:890-899) that 'REQ-103's colony-spawn lock does NOT provide staleness protection for colonySurplusUsd and MUST NOT be cited as though it did' -- the citation is accurate, grounded in REQ-103's actual current prose, and is NOT a false safety net of the FIND-501 kind (which wrongly asserted a homeDir-related property without re-checking the real resolver source first).

Separately, I independently re-spot-checked the iteration-18 8-parameter decideColonySpawn closeout table (reviews/spec/iteration-18/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md) against the CURRENT spec text, not merely trusting the table at face value: colonySurplusUsd (fixed, confirmed above); recentSpawnAttempts (bound via deriveRecentSpawnAttempts, behavioral-spec.md:1028-1032, confirmed unchanged and still bound); childrenProvisioning (bound via countChildrenProvisioning, behavioral-spec.md:1033-1038, confirmed unchanged and still bound); spawnThresholdUsd (a fully-specified two-constant formula, MIN_SHELTER_USD * SAFETY_MARGIN_MULTIPLIER, itself fed by deriveMeasuredShelterCostUsd, behavioral-spec.md:959-977 -- confirmed this formula-shaped derivation does not map cleanly onto the single-function-return-value binding-sentence pattern, and the table's own reasoning for treating it as adequately-derived-elsewhere rather than requiring an identical sentence is sound, not an evasion); nowMs (confirmed a genuine raw wall-clock primitive needing no further derivation, mirroring selectCloudTarget's own established iteration-17 treatment of its four raw price/availability inputs); cooldownDays/failureCooldownCap (confirmed explicit defaults stated at BOTH the EARS level, behavioral-spec.md:854/865, AND the Acceptance-Criteria level, behavioral-spec.md:1014-1017); maxConcurrentSpawns (confirmed the new Acceptance-Criteria-level default clause was actually added, behavioral-spec.md:1017-1019: 'maxConcurrentSpawns defaults to 1, identical to MAX_CONCURRENT_SPAWNS's own default above -- never independently configurable to a different value'). All 8 parameters check out independently against the current spec text -- the closeout table's own conclusions are accurate, not merely asserted.

convergenceSignals.note:
FIND-1701 (iteration 18's critical finding) is genuinely, completely resolved -- both the colonySurplusUsd real-derivation binding itself and the honest (non-false) framing of REQ-103's lock-scope limitation were independently re-verified against the CURRENT spec text, not merely trusted from RESOLUTION-NOTES.md. The decideColonySpawn 8-parameter closeout table (iteration 18's own dedicated mandate) was independently re-spot-checked and matches the builder's own conclusions on all 8 rows -- no residual gap on that specific function's own signature.

HOWEVER, this iteration's own mandated full-spec sweep -- explicitly tasked with checking every OTHER pure function's signature (not just decideColonySpawn) given how many times this general class of defect has now recurred, plus a separate check for entirely different defect classes -- surfaced THREE new findings, none of them on decideColonySpawn itself: FIND-1801 (major) is a closely-related-but-distinct sub-class of the recurring failure -- a bare SCALAR CONSTANT (bootstrapWindowDays) lacking an explicit default plus a by-construction identity proof against its same-meaning sibling constant (REQ-402's BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_DAYS), the same shape this document's own PROP-402e/PROP-206g discipline already resolves for two OTHER cross-requirement pairs but was never applied here, on a SIBLING parameter of the very function (filterProductiveCitizens) whose OTHER two parameters iteration 17 just hardened. FIND-1802 (critical) is the SEVENTH confirmed instance of the exact, already-established recurring class (a complex/derived value's own first-listed, most consequential parameter lacking a 'never hand-assembled, always the direct return value of X()' binding), found this time on computeSpawnGate's balanceAkt rather than any parameter of decideColonySpawn/filterProductiveCitizens/needsSolanaWallet (the three functions this class has previously been found on) -- confirming the failure class extends beyond the REQ-101/102/202 cluster the prior six iterations focused on, into REQ-303's Akash-specific gate as well. FIND-1803 (critical) is a genuinely DIFFERENT class of defect from the pinned-input-derivation pattern entirely: an internal self-contradiction in REQ-303's own text about whether computeSpawnGate's ready:false result should trigger REQ-304's AKT funding bridge or unconditionally abort the deploy attempt before that bridge is ever attempted -- if the more specific, unconditional EARS-styled Edge Case wording is what an implementer follows (the natural reading, since it is the more specific and more recently-stated of the two conflicting sentences), REQ-304's entire Akash AKT-funding mechanism -- the subject of three whole prior fix iterations (FIND-402/502/602) -- would never actually execute in the real orchestration, silently making every AKT-shortfall Akash deploy attempt fail permanently rather than self-fund via the route REQ-304 so carefully documents.

A normal fresh, skeptical pass over the REST of REQ-101 through REQ-403 for entirely different defect classes (money-safety issues, boundary/off-by-one bugs, internally-inconsistent multi-statement requirements of the FIND-1201/1701 kind beyond the one found above, cross-feature staleness, security surface, purity-boundary leaks) found nothing further: the Cooldown Check's success-vs-failure-cap reconciliation, the lock's staggered-race scope (PROP-103e), the dual-chain balance handling (PROP-101f/g/h), the co-funding ceiling logic (PROP-304f/PROP-101i), the wallet re-derivation chain (PROP-105g/h/i), the Nosana secrets-injection path, and the REQ-403 explicit-env/COORDINATOR_HOME discipline all remain internally consistent and adequately proof-obligated on this fresh, full read. This is the EIGHTH total instance (counting both the exact-class recurrences iterations 14-18 found, FIND-1802's continuation of that exact class, and FIND-1801's closely-related scalar-constant sub-class) of a pinned/constant input lacking its own binding discipline being found in this document, PLUS one genuinely new class of defect (FIND-1803) -- future sweeps should specifically (a) extend the classification checklist to cover bare numeric/scalar parameters, not only complex/array-shaped parameters, for the 'explicit default + by-construction identity with any same-meaning sibling constant' treatment, (b) extend the sweep explicitly into REQ群C (REQ-301-306), which iterations 14-18's sweeps concentrated less on than REQ群A/B, and (c) specifically re-read every multi-sentence requirement paragraph that describes a conditional outcome (a 'SHALL treat this as X' clause) against every OTHER sentence in the SAME requirement that describes a related mechanism, checking for the FIND-1803 class of self-contradiction, not only for missing citations.
